title:
Turn everyday
conversations into
continuing care.
lead:
Luklarn helps older adults feel heard
and families stay involved, even from afar.
notes: Start with a familiar feeling: we want to know our parents are well, but cannot always be there. Luklarn turns everyday conversations into information families can follow up on. Click the phone to demonstrate. All data in this presentation is fictional.

eye: The love is there. The information is scattered.
title:
“I took my pills.”
There is still
more to know.
lead:
Meals, symptoms and readings live in different places.
Families have to piece the story together.
features: What happened, and what needs follow-up?
notes: These are design hypotheses, not findings from a completed user study. Validate how often these problems occur and how much they matter. Our starting point is reducing the burden of remembering and collecting information, without claiming clinical outcomes.

title:
Care at home.
A growing need
for families.
lead:
Start with working adults supporting older parents
who need help tracking medication and chronic conditions.
notes: Thailand’s National Statistical Office reported that people aged 60 and over represented20.0% of the population in its2024 Survey of Older Persons. This is population context, not a count of paying customers. The initial customer segment must be specific and its needs validated.

eye: Make technology meet people where they are
title:
Less navigating.
More natural
conversation.
lead:
Older adults speak in their own words.
Luklarn listens, clarifies and helps with the next step.
notes: Play the sample conversation. This is a text-based demo with an animated mascot, not a live microphone session. Show how a conversation becomes a draft, with one explicit confirmation before saving.

eye: Talk and see, in the same call
title:
“What is this?”
Show the label.
Keep talking.
lead:
Read labels and search for information with sources.
When a detail is unclear, Luklarn asks before saving.
notes: The actual app sends periodic camera images to support the conversation, not continuous diagnostic video. This demo does not verify medication names or doses from an image. Blood pressure requires a real measuring device; it is not measured from a face.

title:
Meals. Medicines.
And the things
not to forget.
lead:
Track information relevant to diabetes, blood pressure
and cholesterol through voice, records and a calendar.
features: Separate measured readings from food estimates.
notes: The calendar demo changes only the presentation, not the real database. The app supports voice-controlled calendar actions and confirmed records. Food nutrition is an estimate, not a clinical measurement.

eye: Know what happened. Know what to follow up.
title:
Clear for families.
Ready for a
doctor’s review.
lead:
See key events, times and sources,
alongside open questions and follow-up tasks.
notes: The app stores immutable report snapshots in PostgreSQL with source information. Reviews do not rewrite the original report. Shared links have limited scope and can be revoked. The example shown here is fictional and is not patient advice.

eye: A check-in that comes to you
title:
A familiar voice.
A timely call.
A little care.
lead:
A proposed service beyond the app screen:
scheduled check-ins and medication conversations.
notes: Clearly identify this as a simulated call in the browser. Realtime AI over a phone number is not implemented. The app has a provider adapter and a greeting-only test path. It is not an emergency monitoring service or a staffed escalation service.

title:
Adult children pay.
The whole family
benefits.
lead:
Test recurring family subscriptions
and distribution through clinics and home-care teams.
notes: These are revenue hypotheses. No revenue, customers or partnerships are claimed. Measure willingness to pay, retention, voice AI costs, onboarding and support before setting prices or claiming attractive unit economics.

eye: A working prototype. A path to a pilot.
title:
Prove the care
continues.
Then scale.
lead:
Voice, camera, search and storage are in the prototype.
Next: test with real people and care teams.
features: Successful first conversations and setup support.
Expert review of completeness and sources.
Retention, cost and willingness to pay.
notes: No clinical outcomes or revenue have been validated. Before real service deployment, implement production accounts and roles, test voice and hardware, and review privacy and safety. Start with synthetic-data usability tests before a real-user pilot under appropriate safeguards.

eye: Luklarn. Care for the people we love.
title:
Someone to ask.
Someone to listen.
Every day.
lead:
Co-design a pilot with families,
clinics and home-care teams.
notes: Close by asking for pilot partners and support to test the product. Do not invent a fundraising amount or sales figures. Invite judges and investors to try the phone demo and discuss how to validate value together.
